analysis.title: How will Fed rate hikes impact markets?
key_insights: UBS CIO expects 25 basis point Fed rate hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, and does not expect a measured tightening cycle to derail the US economy or the equity rally.
Strong US data and higher energy costs pushed Treasury yields higher. September CPI came in above consensus, with core CPI at 2.6% y/y.
The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.36% intraday in early October, the highest since 2002, and has since eased to about 4.95%.

The FOMC held rates in October after a 25 basis point hike in September. It upgraded its view of US economic activity to 'strong'. Chair Warsh said financial conditions had tightened and inflation expectations were moving in the right direction.
US GDP growth was close to 2.5% annualized in the first half of 2026 and tracked near 3% in Q3, which supports the view that the economy can absorb a longer period of elevated rates.

UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027, and recommends positioning for further equity gains while diversifying across regions, sectors and return drivers and managing concentrated single-stock exposure.

UBS rates fixed income Attractive and favors medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds and medium-maturity credit from stronger investment grade issuers. It is cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit.

The new orders component of the ISM Manufacturing Index has been in expansion territory for nine consecutive months. Past US downturns generally began at least two years after the Fed started raising rates.

trade_ideas.description: Add selectively to medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds and medium-maturity credit from stronger investment grade issuers, using higher yields to build portfolio income
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher starting yields are creating opportunities to add portfolio income.
trade_ideas.risk: The report is cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit.

trade_ideas.description: Maintain diversified US equity exposure for further gains, spread across regions, sectors and return drivers, and manage concentrated single-stock exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: Resilient earnings and robust growth should help equities withstand moderate policy tightening.

risk_factors: Higher energy costs and strong data could extend the tightening cycle beyond UBS's expected two hikes.
The 10-year yield could move back toward the early-October peak of 5.36%.
Longest-maturity bonds and lower-quality credit are flagged as areas for caution.
Concentrated single-stock exposure needs to be managed.
